["## Learn about COBRA insurance and how to get coverage

- COBRA, the Consolidated Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act, lets qualified workers keep their group health insurance for a limited time after a change in eligibility.", 
"## How does COBRA insurance work?

- COBRA applies to most private sector businesses with 20 or more employees. It requires an employer's group health insurance plan to continue after qualifying life events. These include:
- Termination or a reduction of a covered employee's hours
- Divorce or legal separation from a covered employee
- Death of a covered employee
- Medicare eligibility for a covered employee
- Loss of a child's or dependent's health insurance coverage under the plan
- Qualified beneficiaries under COBRA include:
- An employee
- Spouse
- Former spouses
- Dependent children
- The amount of time COBRA benefits last depends on the qualifying life event you experience. In some cases, it may be for 36 months. If your hours were reduced or your job was terminated, you can receive COBRA benefits for 18 months.", 
"## Find out if you are eligible for COBRA

- COBRA eligibility has three basic requirements that must be met for you to get a continuation of coverage:
- Your group health plan must be covered by COBRA.
- A qualifying event must occur.
- You must be a qualified beneficiary for that event.", 
"## How to get COBRA coverage

When a qualifying life event happens, you or your employer will notify the health plan. The plan will send an election notice that you will have 60 days to respond to. If you elect to take COBRA coverage, your employer may pay a portion of or the full amount of your insurance premium.
- Contact your employer’s health insurance plan administrator with questions about COBRA, including:

Unemployment Insurance 
- What is it? Temporary income when you lose your job (or had hours reduced) through no fault of your own. 
- How much can I get? You get from $40 to $450 each week, depending on how much you earned in the past 18 months. EDD has an Unemployment Benefit Calculator to help you estimate how much you might get before you apply. 
- How long does it take to hear back? It takes about three weeks to process your benefit application and make the first payment. 
- You may also be able to attend school or training while receiving unemployment benefits. Learn more about California Training Benefits here: https://edd.ca.gov/en/unemployment/
- Am I eligible? You need to have all of the following to get unemployment benefits: Social Security number, authorization to work in the US (if not a US citizen), have earned a minimum amount of money over the past 18 months (called base period), be totally or partially unemployed through no fault of your own, and be physically able to, available for and looking for work each week and ready / willing to accept work right away
- What documents you need to make applying faster: 
--Personal Information (SSN, photo ID, other identity documentation like a W2 or bill)
--Past 18 Months of Employment Information (Employer names, mailing and physical addresses, dates worked, total income before taxes and deductions (gross wages), hours worked, and how you were paid (e.g., weekly or monthly)
--Most Recent Employer Information (Employer name, address, and phone number and your immediate supervisor, date you last worked, and total income before taxes and deductions (gross wages) in the last week (Sun - Sat) you worked
--Reason you aren't working or had your hours cut (note: if you voluntarily quit or were fired / let go for misconduct, you may not be able to get benefits) 
--Citizenship (if non-US citizen, you’ll need your USCIS document, such as your Permanent Resident Card, Employment Authorization Card, or Refugee Travel Document) 
--There are additional documents if you worked in federal government or military service in the last 18 months (Notice to Federal Employee About Unemployment Insurance, Standard Form 8 and DD214 Member Copy 4 respectively). 
- How to apply and what to expect? 
Step 1: Get all the information and documents above together. 
Step 2: Apply online on California's EDD website, call by phone 1-800-300-5616 M-F 8am to 5pm PT or apply by fax or mail 
Step 3: After you apply, you have 21 days to sign up for and upload your resume to CalJOBS. 
Step 4: Review Benefit Documents - 2 weeks after you apply, California EDD may ask for more information. They will also send you key documents about your benefits. Details below: 
Notice of Unemployment Insurance Claim Filed (DE 1101CLMT): This is a summary of your claim information. It explains how to correct any errors to avoid payment delays.
Employment Development Department Customer Account Number Notification (DE 5614): This has your EDD Customer Account Number (EDDCAN) to register in UI Online, after you visit myEDD. The EDDCAN also helps verify your account if you speak with an EDD representative. Don’t lose it.
Notice of Unemployment Insurance Award (DE 429Z): This form explains what benefits you can expect, and how to avoid payment delays. If any information is wrong, follow the instructions and appeal in writing within 30 days to avoid payment delays.
Unemployment Insurance Benefits: What You Need to Know (DE 1275B): This provides you a link to a document that explains how you can avoid payment delays by accurately certifying for benefits every two weeks.
Continued Claim (DE 4581): You can use this form to certify by paper, but the process is much slower. Save time and do it online at myEDD or by phone. You’ll certify for benefits every two weeks.
Request for Identity Verification (DE 1326C): If you applied by phone, fax, or mail (or we can’t immediately verify your identity), you’ll receive this form. Visit Respond to Your Request for Identity Verification to learn how to avoid further delays.
Step 5: Certify for Benefits - you need to answer some basic questions every 2 weeks to tell EDD that you are still unemployed but actively looking. Keep an eye out for an email / mail from EDD when it's time. It's fastest to certify online through myEDD, but you can also call 1-866-333-4606 for English and Spanish or by mail (your payments may take longer by mail)
Step 6: Receive Your First Payment - generally takes 3 weeks after you submit your application up to getting your first payment. You can get it by direct deposit, debit card or mailed check. 
Step 7: Keep Certifying - you must do this step 5 every 2 weeks to keep your benefits 
Step 8: End Your Benefits: your benefit year ends 12 months after the start date of your first claim. You will need to re-apply if you still meet eligibility criteria.

["## Learn about COBRA insurance and how to get coverage

- COBRA, the Consolidated Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act, lets qualified workers keep their group health insurance for a limited time after a change in eligibility.", 
"## How does COBRA insurance work?

- COBRA applies to most private sector businesses with 20 or more employees. It requires an employer's group health insurance plan to continue after qualifying life events. These include:
- Termination or a reduction of a covered employee's hours
- Divorce or legal separation from a covered employee
- Death of a covered employee
- Medicare eligibility for a covered employee
- Loss of a child's or dependent's health insurance coverage under the plan
- Qualified beneficiaries under COBRA include:
- An employee
- Spouse
- Former spouses

## Unemployment Insurance (UI)
You may still qualify for UI benefits while receiving severance and doing part-time work. Here's what you need to know:

**Severance Pay**
- Must report severance pay to EDD
- May reduce your weekly UI benefit amount
- Different rules apply based on how severance is paid (lump sum vs. periodic)

**Part-time/Gig Work**
- You can work part-time while on UI
- Must report all earnings each week
- Benefits reduced for partial earnings
- Still must be available for full-time work
- Must actively seek full-time employment

## Medi-Cal
Good news - you may qualify for Medi-Cal even with some income:

- Income limits based on household size and income type
- Severance and part-time earnings count as income
- Monthly income limits are higher than traditional Medi-Cal through expanded coverage

## Required Documentation
- Pay stubs/proof of earnings
- Severance agreement
- ID and Social Security card
- California address verification

## Additional Programs to Consider
- [CalFresh (food assistance)](https://www.cdss.ca.gov/calfresh)
- Covered California (if income too high for Medi-Cal)
- [Job search assistance through America's Job Center](https://www.careeronestop.org/LocalHelp/AmericanJobCenters/find-american-job-centers.aspx)

1. File UI claim immediately at [UI Online](https://edd.ca.gov/unemployment)
2. Apply for Medi-Cal through [Covered California](https://www.coveredca.com/)
3. Report all income changes to both programs
4. Keep detailed records of your job search

Remember: Benefits and eligibility can vary by county. Contact your local county office for specific details about Medi-Cal eligibility in your area.

You can get this benefit if: you have a valid CA driver's license, own a vehicle valued at $25K or less, be at least 16 years old, have a good driving record, and meet income requirements (based on your husband's income, you all likely qualify for this as the max pre tax annual income limit is $107,875 for a household of 6). 
Documents you would need to provde: driver's license, current vehicle registration, initial deposit for payment, and one document for proof of income such any beneift letter from other California programs like CalFresh, CalWORKS, Lifeline, etc. or income tax returns, W-2, 1099, or payroll stub, etc.)

For health coverage, California offers Medi-Cal or Medicaid which is free or low-cost health care to people who qualify. For those who make above Medi-Cal income limits, Covered California is another option to get help paying for a private healthcare plan. 

## Medi-Cal Details
What Medi-Cal covers: 
- pays for doctor visits
- hospital care
- immunization (vaccines) 
- pregnancy related help 
- nursing home care and more 

Eligibility: You have to live in California and meet certain rules like income cut-offs based on household size (138% of the federal poverty level or lower, which is $59,547 for a household of 6). Even if your income is over the Medi-Cal limit, you could still get help paying for private health care through Covered California. You can qualify even if you are not a US citizen or national. 

How to apply: 
- Go in person to your county office (if you tell me your county, I can look this up for you) or online on BenefitsCal.com.
- To make the application faster, spend some time gathering these documents first, typically 1 or 2 in each category: 
    - Identity: birth certificate, driver's license, SSN, paycheck, US passport, military ID, etc. 
    - Immigration Status: INS documents, immigration papers/forms/cards, certificate of naturalization, etc. 
    - Proof you live in California: driver's license, check stub, rent/mortgage receipt, utility bill, etc.
    - Money you earn: check stubs for last 30 days, statement from employer, last year's tax return, bank statement for direct deposit 
    - Other income: benefit check, copies of child support checks, alimony, award letters 
    - Resources: bank statements showing savings / checkings accounts, mortgage statements, vehicle registration, etc. 
    - Additional proof of coverage: information about any job related health insurance that is open to your or your family, policy numbers of any current plans 

How long does it take?

If you have a disability it may take up to 90 days (depending on how quickly you submit documents and doctors submit records. To speed up the process, tell your county office that you have an urgent medical or dental need. This can be a serious illness or also if you are pregnant. 

Using and Keeping your coverage:

- You have to renew your benefits every year on the anniversary of your enrollment in Medi-Cal. The county may automatically renew you or you may need to provide additional information if not. They will mail you a letter telling you what they need. Log in to your account to find out your renewal date. It's good to put a reminder in your calendar a year from when you apply and get approved as a reminder. 

## Covered California Details
Eligibility: Anyone can apply for Covered California if you are a California resident and have satisfactory immigration status. The most financial help is available for people who are within 138% to 250% of the federal poverty level ($59,547 to $107,875 for a household of 6), but even individuals making up to 400% of the federal poverty level could get help.If you are already receiving health insurance, you can still get a plan but may not be able to get help covering the plan costs. DACA recipients do not qualify. People who are not lawfully present do not qualify. People over 65 usually do not as well (they are Medicare eligible). 

How to apply: Applying online is fastest (takes about 30 minutes) on coveredca.com. You can also get free help locally from a certified enroller or apply by phone (takes abuot 1 hour). You can also complete a paper application and mail it in but processing may take a bit longer. 
Gathering these documents ahead of time can make the application process go faster: 
Covered California compares information you put in your application with government data sources. If the data does not match, Covered California will need additional documents from you such as the following: proof of income, SSN, identity, citizenship / immigration status, proof of lack of minimum essential health coverage (this can be a certificate from an insurance company showing end date of your previous coverage, an employer statement saying they no longer offer this kind of health coverage, etc.). Keeping your benefits:

Renewal is in the fall of each year and goes to the end of the calendar year. You'll get notified by Covered California when it's time. 


## COBRA insurance 
COBRA is another temporary option for health coverage. It applies to most private companies with 20 or more employees. It requires that the employer's group health insurance plan continues after qualifying life events such as: 
- Termination of reduction in employee hours 
- Divorce or legal separation from a covered employee
- Death of an employee
- Medicare eligibility for a employee
- Loss of a child or dependent's health coverage under the plan 
How long do COBRA benefits last? 
This depends on the qualifying life event. Some times this is 36 months or 3 years. If you are on COBRA because your employer reduced your hours or terminated your job, you could receive COBRA for 18 months or 1.5 years. 
Eligibility for COBRA:

- A qualifying life event must occur 
- You must be a qualified beneficiary for the event.

See if your drug has a generic version - this is the same formulation but with a different brand that is usually more affordable. You can also go to your county social service agency to get referrals to local health centers and nonprofits that may be able to help you.

"## How does COBRA insurance work?

- COBRA applies to most private sector businesses with 20 or more employees. It requires an employer's group health insurance plan to continue after qualifying life events. These include:
- Termination or a reduction of a covered employee's hours
- Divorce or legal separation from a covered employee
- Death of a covered employee
- Medicare eligibility for a covered employee
- Loss of a child's or dependent's health insurance coverage under the plan
- Qualified beneficiaries under COBRA include:
- An employee
- Spouse
- Former spouses
- Dependent children
- The amount of time COBRA benefits last depends on the qualifying life event you experience. In some cases, it may be for 36 months. If your hours were reduced or your job was terminated, you can receive COBRA benefits for 18 months.", 
"## Find out if you are eligible for COBRA

- Your group health plan must be covered by COBRA.

- Death of a covered employee

- Loss of a child's or dependent's health insurance coverage under the plan

- An employee

I'm sorry to hear that, job loss is very stressful. I'm here to help. Here are some options based on what you shared so far. I can go into more detail into any of these. 

First, you can call 2-1-1 to get connected to resources any time (for help finding childcare, affordable housing, cash help, healthcare and more). 
Findhelp.org is a great search tool to find local resources near your zip code to find local food pantries, meal programs, and support for housing, financial assistance, health care, and more. 

Food Help 
- If you need food now, you can go to the San Diego Food Bank on 9850 Distribution Avenue or call ahead first to see if you qualify for help: 858-527-1419
- Apply for SNAP (food stamps), called CalFresh in California. If eligible, you can get monthly help paying for groceries. 
CalFresh Steps to Apply: 
- You can apply on BenefitsCal.com or go to your county office. Online chat support is available M-F 9am to 4pm PT. 
- Your county will call within 1-2 weeks for an interview and will let you know within 30 days if you're approved. Sounds like you need help sooner, so definitely ask for faster help (expedited review) when you apply. 
- If approved, you will get your EBT card for groceries within 10 days. It gets refilled monthly. 
- Documents you need: copy of your ID, proof of any income, proof of immigration status (for non-citizens) within 30 days of applying. Other optional documents could increase you benefit amount like proof of housing expenses, child support, or dependent care, and proof of medical expenses if you are disabled. Highly recommend you include this if you have any costs related to your disability. 

Healthcare
For health coverage, California offers Medi-Cal or Medicaid which is free or low-cost health care to people who qualify. For those who make above Medi-Cal income limits, Covered California is another option to get help paying for a private healthcare plan. 

## Medi-Cal Details
What Medi-Cal covers: 
- pays for doctor visits
- hospital care
- immunization (vaccines) 
- pregnancy related help 
- nursing home care and more 

Eligibility: You have to live in California and meet certain rules like income cut-offs based on household size (138% of the federal poverty level or lower, which is $21,597 for a household of 1). Even if your income is over the Medi-Cal limit, you could still get help paying for private health care through Covered California. You can qualify even if you are not a US citizen or national. 

How to apply: 
- Go in person to your county office (if you tell me your county, I can look this up for you) or online on BenefitsCal.com.
- To make the application faster, spend some time gathering these documents first, typically 1 or 2 in each category: 
    - Identity: birth certificate, driver's license, SSN, paycheck, US passport, military ID, etc. 
    - Immigration Status: INS documents, immigration papers/forms/cards, certificate of naturalization, etc. 
    - Proof you live in California: driver's license, check stub, rent/mortgage receipt, utility bill, etc.
    - Money you earn: check stubs for last 30 days, statement from employer, last year's tax return, bank statement for direct deposit 
    - Other income: benefit check, copies of child support checks, alimony, award letters 
    - Resources: bank statements showing savings / checkings accounts, mortgage statements, vehicle registration, etc. 
    - Additional proof of coverage: information about any job related health insurance that is open to your or your family, policy numbers of any current plans 

How long does it take? 
- California must decide on your case within 45 days. You may hear back sooner. If you have a disability it may take up to 90 days (depending on how quickly you submit documents and doctors submit records. To speed up the process, tell your county office that you have an urgent medical or dental need. This can be a serious illness or also if you are pregnant. 

Using and Keeping your coverage: 
- If approved, you'll get a Benefits Identification Card (BIC) in the mail. You can start using Medi-Cal right away. To get all benefits, you may need to pick a Medi-Cal health plan. Your county will mail you details about plans and how to sign up. 
- If anything changes in your situation like moving, income amount, number of people in your home, pregnancy, or marital status, you need to update your application within 10 days. 
- You have to renew your benefits every year on the anniversary of your enrollment in Medi-Cal. The county may automatically renew you or you may need to provide additional information if not. They will mail you a letter telling you what they need. Log in to your account to find out your renewal date. It's good to put a reminder in your calendar a year from when you apply and get approved as a reminder. 

## COBRA insurance 
COBRA is another temporary option for health coverage. It applies to most private companies with 20 or more employees. It requires that the employer's group health insurance plan continues after qualifying life events such as: 
- Termination of reduction in employee hours 
- Divorce or legal separation from a covered employee
- Death of an employee
- Medicare eligibility for a employee
- Loss of a child or dependent's health coverage under the plan 
How long do COBRA benefits last? 
This depends on the qualifying life event. Some times this is 36 months or 3 years. If you are on COBRA because your employer reduced your hours or terminated your job, you could receive COBRA for 18 months or 1.5 years. 
Eligibility for COBRA: 
- Your group health plan must be covered by COBRA
- A qualifying life event must occur 
- You must be a qualified beneficiary for the event. 
How to Get COBRA: 
- Your employer notifies your health plan when a qualifying life event happens.
- Keep an eye out for an election notice from the health plan - you will have 60 days to respond to it. 
- If you accept the COBRA coverage, your employer may pay some or the full amount of your monthly premium. 
If you have questions, you should contact your employer's health insurance plan administrator. 

## Help with Medical Bills
There are also options for help with medical bills even if you don't have insurance or are under-insured (you have healthcare needs that are not covered by your plan): 
After applying for Medicaid (Medi-Cal) and ACA Marketplace (Covered California), and you still need help covering health care costs, you can still get help through the following: 
- Charity care: in most cases, you can apply through the doctor office or hospital where you are seeking medical treatment. Take these steps: 
    - First, ask for a copy of the hosital or provider's financial assistance policy. 
    - Fill out the application with information about your income and expenses 
    - Ask questions about the process like how long it will take to process your application and what happens to your bill in the meantime
    - Notify debt collectors if they are trying to collect and ask them to pause while that is pending 
    - Follow up with the hospital / provider and its billing department about your application's status as needed. 
- Medicare has several savings and extra help options - but this only applies if you are Medicare eligible - usually 65 years or older 
- Debt management: Get on a payment schedule with a credit counselor. You make an account with the credit counseling organization and then pay off your debt as you deposit money. You may get lower interest rates and certain fees waived when going this route. 
- Prescription costs: You can contact the pharmaceutical companies that make your drugs or devices and ask about low cost options, samples or discounts. See if your drug has a generic version - this is the same formulation but with a different brand that is usually more affordable. You can also go to your county social service agency to get referrals to local health centers and nonprofits that may be able to help you. 

Cash Aid (CalWORKs and General Assistance) 
- CalWORKs helps with cash to pay for rent, housing, food, clothing, medical payments, and utilities for families with at least one child in the home. ## Can You Receive More Than One Type of Assistance at the same time?

**Yes.** In California many public‑assistance programs can be received together.  
However, each program has its own rules about how income, assets, and other benefits are counted. Some programs **coordinate** with each other, while others may limit the amount you can receive.

Below is a quick guide to the most common combinations, what you’ll need to know, and the steps to apply.

---

## Common Program Pairings

| Programs that can often be combined | How they interact | Typical extra paperwork |
|--------------------------------------|-------------------|--------------------------|
| **Unemployment Insurance (UI)** + **CalWORKs** (cash aid) | UI benefits are usually **not counted** as income for CalWORKs, so you can receive both. | UI award letter, CalWORKs application. |
| **CalWORKs** + **CalFresh** (food stamps) | CalFresh counts a portion of CalWORKs cash as income, but you can still qualify for a reduced benefit. | CalWORKs award notice, CalFresh application. |
| **CalFresh** + **Medi‑Cal** (health coverage) | CalFresh eligibility is **not affected** by Medi‑Cal enrollment. | Proof of residency, income, and identity for each program. |
| **General Assistance (GA)** + **SSI/SSDI** | GA can supplement the low federal SSI/SSDI payments, but the total must stay under the GA income limit. | SSI award letter, GA application. |
| **Housing Assistance (Section 8, Vouchers, or Public Housing)** + **CalWORKs/CalFresh** | Housing subsidies are usually **not counted** as income for cash or food programs. | Lease agreement, voucher paperwork, CalWORKs/CalFresh forms. |
| **Disability Benefits (DI, SSI)** + **CalFresh** | Disability income is counted, but many people still qualify for food assistance. | Disability award letter, CalFresh application. |

> **Note:** Exact rules can vary **by county** (e.g., some counties have stricter income‑counting methods for CalWORKs). Always check with your local Human Services Agency (HSA) for the most accurate guidance.

## Applying for Medi‑Cal after a layoff  

I’m sorry you’re going through this. Below is a simple guide to help you start a Medi‑Cal application in California.

---

### 1. What is Medi‑Cal?  
- **Medi‑Cal** is California’s Medicaid program.  
- It provides free or low‑cost health coverage for people with limited income and resources.  
- If you lost your job, you may qualify right away because your household income has dropped.

---

### 2. Basic eligibility (general rules)  

| Factor | Typical requirement | Note |
|--------|--------------------|------|
| **Income** | Usually ≤ 138 % of the Federal Poverty Level (FPL). After a layoff many people fall under this limit. | Exact dollar amount changes each year; the online calculator will tell you if you qualify. |
| **Residency** | Must live in California. | Provide proof of address. |
| **Citizenship/Immigration** | U.S. citizens, nationals, or qualified immigrants (e.g., green‑card holders, refugees). | Some non‑citizens have limited eligibility; the application will ask the details. |
| **Resources** | Most adults have a $2,000 limit on countable assets (cash, bank accounts, etc.). | Some groups (e.g., seniors, people with disabilities) have higher limits. |
| **Other coverage** | If you have other health insurance, you may still be eligible, but you’ll need to report it. | |

*Eligibility rules can vary a little by **county**, especially for resource limits and special programs. Your county social services office can confirm the exact numbers for you.*

---

### 3. Steps to apply  

1. **Gather needed documents** (see the list below).  
2. **Create an online account** at **[Covered California – Medi‑Cal enrollment](https://www.coveredca.com/medi-cal/)** or call the state’s toll‑free line **1‑800‑300‑1506**.  
3. **Complete the application** – you can do it:  
   - **Online** (fastest).  
   - **By phone** with a representative.  
   - **In person** at your local County Social Services Office (CSSO).  
4. **Submit supporting documents** (upload online, fax, mail, or bring in person).  
5. **Wait for a decision** – most counties process applications within **30 days**. You’ll receive a notice by mail or email.  
6. **If approved**, you’ll get a Medi‑Cal card and can choose a doctor or health plan.  

---

### 4. Documents you’ll need  

| Category | Examples |
|----------|----------|
| **Proof of identity** | Driver’s license, state ID, passport, or birth certificate. |
| **Proof of California residency** | Utility bill, lease/rental agreement, or mortgage statement (showing your name and address). |
| **Income information** | Recent pay stub (if you still have one), final pay stub from your employer, unemployment insurance (UI) award letter, or a copy of your most recent tax return. |
| **Bank/asset statements** | Recent bank account statement (to show assets under $2,000). |
| **Immigration status (if not a citizen)** | Green card, work permit (EAD), or other immigration document. |
| **Other health coverage** (if any) | Insurance card or notice of coverage termination. |

*If you can’t get a particular document right away, let the caseworker know. They often accept a written explanation and will let you submit the missing item later.*

---

### 5. Timelines you should expect  

| Action | Typical time frame |
|--------|-------------------|
| **Application submission** | Immediate (online) or same‑day (in‑person/phone). |
| **Initial review** | 7‑14 days (county may request more info). |
| **Final decision** | Up to **30 days** from complete submission. |
| **Receiving the Medi‑Cal card** | 7‑10 days after approval (mail). |
| **Choosing a health plan** | You have **30 days** after receiving the card to pick a plan; you can also keep the default plan. |

If you need health care right away, ask the caseworker about **emergency coverage** while your application is pending.

---

### 6. County‑specific notes  

- **Every county runs its own CSSO**, so office hours, in‑person locations, and some resource limits can differ.  
- Some counties offer **“Rapid Access”** programs that can give you temporary coverage within a few days. Call your local office to ask.  
- You can find your county office here: **[County Social Services Offices](https://www.cdss.ca.gov/County-Offices)**.

---

### 7. Other programs that may help right now  

| Program | What it does | How to apply |
|---------|--------------|--------------|
| **Unemployment Insurance (UI)** | Weekly cash benefits while you look for work. | Apply online at **[EDD UI Online](https://edd.ca.gov/Unemployment/UI_Online.htm)**. |
| **CalFresh (SNAP)** | Monthly food assistance. | Apply at the same CSSO or online at **[GetCalFresh.org](https://www.getcalfresh.org/)**. |
| **California Work Opportunity and Responsibility to Kids (CalWORKs)** | Cash aid for families with children. | Same CSSO; ask the caseworker. |
| **General Relief (GR)** | Short‑term cash help for adults without other aid. | County CSSO. |
| **Low‑Income Health Programs (e.g., Covered California subsidies)** | If you earn a little more than Medi‑Cal limits, you may qualify for premium subsidies. | Apply through **[Covered California](https://www.coveredca.com/)**. |
| **Medical Bill Assistance** | Help paying existing medical bills while you wait for coverage. | Look for local non‑profits or ask your hospital’s financial assistance office. |

---

### 8. Quick checklist before you start  

- [ ] Write down your **full name, address, phone, and email**.  
- [ ] List **all sources of income** (including UI, part‑time work, or severance).  
- [ ] Gather the documents in the table above.  
- [ ] Find your **county CSSO phone number** (link above).  
- [ ] Set aside **30 minutes** for the online application (you can pause and return).  

---

### 9. Need help?  

- **Phone:** 1‑800‑300‑1506 (Medi‑Cal enrollment line, 24 hrs).  
- **In‑person:** Locate your nearest County Social Services Office.  
- **Online chat:** Available on the Covered California site.  

You’re not alone—many people apply for Medi‑Cal after a layoff, and the system is set up to help you quickly. Take one step at a time, and let the caseworker know if anything is unclear. Good luck, and take care of yourself during this transition.

## Unemployment Insurance (UI) in California  

**Unemployment Insurance does not have a fixed “income limit.”**  
Instead, the amount you may receive is calculated from the wages you earned during your **base period** (the first four of the last five completed calendar quarters before you filed a claim).  

### How UI Benefits Are Determined  

| Factor | What It Means for You |
|--------|-----------------------|
| **Base‑period earnings** | The more you earned in the base period, the higher your weekly benefit amount (WBA). |
| **Maximum weekly benefit** | In 2025 the state‑wide maximum WBA is **$450** per week (subject to change each year). |
| **Minimum weekly benefit** | The minimum WBA is **$40** per week. |
| **Duration of benefits** | Up to **26 weeks** of regular UI, with possible extensions during high‑unemployment periods. |

> **Note:** Exact benefit amounts are calculated by the Employment Development Department (EDD) when you file your claim. There is no “income ceiling” that disqualifies you; you simply receive a benefit based on your past earnings.

### Basic Eligibility Requirements  

- **You must be unemployed through no fault of your own** (e.g., layoff, reduction in hours).  
- **You must have earned enough wages** during the base period (generally at least $1,300 total and $1,250 in the highest‑earning quarter).  
- **You must be able, available, and actively seeking work**.

## Unemployment Insurance (UI) – Quick Guide  

**You can apply for UI online, by phone, or by mail.** Below is a simple checklist of what you’ll need and the steps to get started.

| What you need | Why it’s needed |
|---------------|-----------------|
| **Social Security number** | To verify your identity |
| **Driver’s license or state ID** | Proof of identity |
| **Last employer’s name, address, and phone number** | To confirm your work history |
| **Dates you worked and the total wages you earned** (pay stubs, W‑2, or final pay statement) | To calculate your weekly benefit amount |
| **Bank account and routing number** (if you want direct deposit) | To get your benefits faster |
| **Mailing address and phone number** | For any follow‑up questions |
| **If you were a contractor or gig worker:** your 1099‑NEC or 1099‑K forms | UI can cover some self‑employment situations |

### How to Apply  

1. **Create an account on UI Online** – go to the California Employment Development Department (EDD) website:  
   [UI Online – Apply for Unemployment](https://edd.ca.gov/Unemployment/UI_Online.htm)  

2. **Complete the application** – answer the questions about your recent work, earnings, and personal information.  

3. **Submit supporting documents** (if EDD asks for them). You can upload PDFs or photos directly in the portal, or mail them to the address shown on the screen.  

4. **Choose how you want to receive payments** – direct deposit is the fastest, but you can also get a debit card.  

5. **File your first weekly claim** (called a “certification”) within the first week after you apply. This tells EDD you are still unemployed and able to work.  

6. **Keep a record** of the confirmation number you receive after you submit the application. You’ll need it if you call for help.  

### Timelines (Typical)  

| Step | Approximate time |
|------|------------------|
| Application submitted | **Within a few minutes** (online) |
| Initial review by EDD | **1–2 weeks** (you’ll get a notice by mail or email) |
| First benefit payment (if approved) | **Within 7–10 days** after your first weekly certification |
| Weekly certifications | **Every 2 weeks** (you must certify to keep receiving benefits) |

> **Note:** UI is a state program, so the basic rules are the same across California. However, some counties have local job‑search resources or workshops that can help you meet the “work‑search” requirement. Check with your **County Workforce Development Board** for any extra steps they may require.

### Other Programs You Might Qualify For  

Even if you’re only looking for UI now, you may also be eligible for these California assistance programs:

| Program | Who can apply | What it helps with |
|---------|---------------|--------------------|
| **CalWORKs** (Cash Assistance) | Low‑income families with children | Monthly cash aid, childcare, job training |
| **CalFresh** (SNAP) | Residents with limited income | Grocery assistance |
| **Medi‑Cal** (Health Coverage) | Low‑income adults, children, seniors, pregnant people | Free or low‑cost health care |
| **General Assistance (GA)** | Adults without dependents who don’t qualify for other cash aid | Small cash payments for basic needs |
| **Housing Assistance (Section 8, Emergency Rentals)** | Low‑income households | Rental subsidies, emergency shelter |

You can apply for many of these programs **online** at the California Department of Social Services portal:  
[Benefits CalWIN/CalWIN Online](https://benefitscalwin.org/)

### Helpful Tips  

* **Apply as soon as possible.** Benefits are not retroactive beyond a short “waiting week.”  
* **Keep a copy of everything you submit.** If EDD asks for more information, you’ll have it ready.  
* **Report any work you do, even part‑time or gig work.** Not reporting can delay or stop benefits.  
* **If you have trouble with the online system**, you can call the UI claims line: **1‑800‑300‑5616** (Monday‑Friday, 8 am‑5 pm PT).  

---

**You’re not alone.** Many Californians go through this process, and the state offers free resources to help you stay on track. If you need more detailed help, your local **County Workforce Development Board** can walk you through the steps and answer any questions. Good luck, and take it one step at a time!

## What is the Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC)?

The **Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC)** is a federal tax credit that helps low‑ to moderate‑income workers keep more of the money they earn.  
California also offers a **California Earned Income Tax Credit (CalEITC)** that adds extra money on top of the federal credit for eligible residents.

- **It is not a benefit you apply for separately.** You claim it when you file your federal (and state) income tax return.  
- The credit can reduce the amount of tax you owe, and if the credit is larger than your tax bill, you get a **refund**.

---

## Who may be eligible? (Simple checklist)

| Requirement | What to look for |
|-------------|------------------|
| **Age** | You must be at least 25 years old (or have a qualifying child). |
| **Filing status** | Must file a federal tax return (single, head of household, married filing jointly, or qualifying widow(er)). You cannot claim the credit if you file “Married Filing Separately.” |
| **Earned income** | Income from wages, salaries, tips, self‑employment, or certain disability payments. |
| **Investment income** | Must be **$10,000 or less** for the year (this limit is set each year by the IRS). |
| **Qualifying children** *(if you have any)* | Each child must be under 19 (or under 24 if a full‑time student) and meet residency, relationship, and joint return rules. |
| **Social Security numbers** | You, your spouse (if filing jointly), and any qualifying children must have valid SSNs. |
| **California residency** | To get CalEITC, you must be a California resident for the tax year. |

> **Note:** Exact income limits change each year. The IRS and California Franchise Tax Board (FTB) publish the current tables for the tax year you are filing (2025 tax year, filed in 2026). Check the latest tables on their websites.

---

## How to claim the credit

1. **Gather your documents**  
   - All **W‑2** forms from employers.  
   - Any **1099‑NEC** or **1099‑MISC** if you did freelance or contract work.  
   - **Social Security numbers** for you, your spouse (if filing jointly), and any qualifying children.  
   - A copy of last year’s tax return (helps if you’re using the same filing method).  

2. **Choose a filing method**  
   - **Free Online**: Use the IRS Free File program or CalFile (California’s free state filing tool). Both guide you through the EITC questions.  
   - **Tax‑preparer**: If you prefer help, look for a VITA (Volunteer Income Tax Assistance) site near you. VITA volunteers are trained to handle EITC.  

3. **Complete the EITC worksheet** (the software or preparer will do this).  
   - Answer questions about earned income, investment income, and any qualifying children.  
   - The program will calculate the federal EITC amount and, if you qualify, the CalEITC amount.  

4. **File your federal return** (Form 1040) **and** your California state return (Form 540 or 540‑NR).  
   - The credit is applied automatically; you do **not** need a separate form.  

5. **Receive your refund**  
   - If the credit exceeds the tax you owe, the excess is sent to you as a **refund**.  
   - You can choose direct deposit (fastest) or a paper check.  

---

## Timeline

| Action | Approximate deadline |
|--------|----------------------|
| **Gather documents** | As soon as you receive them (usually by end of January). |
| **File federal & state returns** | **April 15 2026** (or the next business day if the 15th falls on a weekend/holiday). |
| **Refund timing** | Direct deposit: 2‑3 weeks after the IRS accepts your return. Paper check: 4‑6 weeks. |
| **Amended return** | If you discover an error, you can file Form 1040‑X within **3 years** of the original filing date. |

---

## Other programs that may help while you’re looking for work

| Program | Who can apply | What it can do for you |
|---------|---------------|------------------------|
| **Unemployment Insurance (UI)** | Recently laid‑off workers who earned enough wages in the base period. | Weekly cash benefits while you search for a new job. |
| **CalWORKs (California Work Opportunity and Responsibility to Kids)** | Low‑income families with children. | Cash aid, job‑training, childcare assistance. |
| **CalFresh (SNAP)** | Low‑income households. | Monthly food benefits that can be used at grocery stores. |
| **Medi‑Cal** | Residents with limited income and assets. | Free or low‑cost health coverage. |
| **California Paid Family Leave (PFL)** | Workers who need time off to care for a seriously ill family member or bond with a new child. | Partial wage replacement for up to 8 weeks. |
| **Local Workforce Development Boards** | Anyone seeking job training or placement services. | Free job‑search assistance, resume workshops, training programs. |

> **County variation:** Many of these programs (especially CalWORKs, CalFresh, and Medi‑Cal) are administered at the county level, so eligibility rules and application processes can differ slightly from one county to another. Contact your **County Human Services Agency** for the exact steps in your area.

---

## Where to get help

- **IRS Free File & CalFile** – file online for free:  
  - Federal: <https://www.irs.gov/filing/free-file-do-your-federal-taxes-for-free>  
  - California: <https://www.ftb.ca.gov/file/personal/calfile.html>

- **VITA (Volunteer Income Tax Assistance)** – find a local site: <https://www.irs.gov/individuals/free-tax-return-preparation>

- **California Department of Social Services – CalWORKs & CalFresh**: <https://www.cdss.ca.gov/>

- **California Employment Development Department (UI & PFL)**: <https://edd.ca.gov/>

- **County Human Services Agency** – search “[Your County] Human Services Agency” for local contact info.

---

### Quick checklist for you

- [ ] Collect all W‑2s and 1099s.  
- [ ] Verify Social Security numbers for everyone on the return.  
- [ ] Use IRS Free File or a VITA site to prepare your return.  
- [ ] Answer the EITC questions carefully; the software will calculate both federal and CalEITC.  
- [ ] File by **April 15 2026** to get any refund as soon as possible.  
- [ ] Explore UI, CalFresh, Medi‑Cal, and local workforce services while you job‑search.

["## General Assistance or General Relief

[""## Housing and Homelessness Programs

The Housing and Homelessness Division (HHD) is within the California Department of Social Services (CDSS). The Division is responsible for program development and oversight of statewide housing programs funded by the CDSS. The Division also serves as a statewide technical assistance provider to all of California’s social services agencies. [""## CalWORKs Housing Support Program (HSP)

The CalWORKs Housing Support Program (HSP) fosters housing stability for families experiencing and at risk of homelessness. HSP assists CalWORKs families who are experiencing or at-risk of homelessness in obtaining permanent housing and can provide temporary shelter, help with moving costs, short to medium-term rental subsidies, and wraparound case management.""],
[""## CalWORKs Homeless Assistance (HA)

The CalWORKs Homeless Assistance (HA) Program aims to help CalWORKs families meet the costs of securing or maintaining permanent housing or emergency shelter. The CalWORKs HA program serves eligible CalWORKs recipients, or apparently eligible CalWORKs applicants, who are homeless or at risk of homelessness. CalWORKs HA can provide payments for temporary shelter once every 12 months with exceptions, as well as payments to secure or maintain housing, including a security deposit and last month’s rent, or up to two months of rent arrearages.""],

[""## Weatherizing Your Home

Having a high energy bill is not the only indicator that you may benefit from energy efficient weatherization measures. If you notice cold drafts in your home from windows or doors, run the heater throughout the entire day in the winter, or run your air conditioner throughout the entire day in the summer, then you may benefit from having an assessment done on your home. An assessment, or energy audit, is performed by community partners in low-income households to find ways to make your home more energy efficient. Some of the energy efficiency improvements include:
- Sealing holes and cracks around doors, windows, and pipes
- Checking that your home is properly insulated
- Repairing or replacing windows
- Checking that heating and air conditioning systems run smoothly
- Repairing or replacing water heaters""],

## How Unemployment Insurance (UI) Works in California  

| **What it is** | A temporary cash benefit for workers who lose a job through no fault of their own. |
|----------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Who runs it** | The California Employment Development Department (EDD). |
| **How long you can receive it** | Up to **26 weeks** in most cases, with possible extensions during statewide emergencies. |
| **How the amount is set** | Based on your **highest‑earning quarter** in the “base period” (the first four of the last five completed quarters). The weekly benefit is a percentage of that earnings, up to a state‑wide maximum. |

### Basic Eligibility Checklist  

- **You were employed in California** and earned enough wages during the base period.  
- **You lost your job** (or had a reduction in hours) **through no fault of your own** (e.g., layoff, reduction, or certain medical reasons).  
- You are **able, available, and actively looking for work**.  
- You are **legally authorized to work** in the U.S.  

> **Note:** Some eligibility details (e.g., “partial unemployment” rules) can vary by county. Your local EDD office can confirm any county‑specific requirements.

---

## Steps to Apply  

1. **Gather Required Documents**  
   - Your **Social Security number**.  
   - Your **driver’s license or ID card number**.  
   - Your **most recent employer’s name, address, and phone number**.  
   - Your **last pay stub** or **W‑2** (to verify earnings).  
   - **Bank account information** for direct deposit (optional but faster).  

2. **Create an Online Account**  
   - Go to the EDD’s UI portal: [UI Online](https://edd.ca.gov/Unemployment/UI_Online.htm).  
   - Follow the prompts to set up a **Secure Access** login.  

3. **File Your Initial Claim**  
   - Complete the **UI claim form** online (or by phone if you cannot access the internet).  
   - Answer all questions truthfully; missing information can delay payment.  

4. **Certify Weekly (or Bi‑weekly) Benefits**  
   - After your claim is approved, you must **certify** each week you want payment.  
   - Report any **earnings**, **job‑search activities**, and **availability for work**.  

5. **Respond to Any EDD Requests**  
   - The EDD may ask for additional proof (e.g., a separation notice).  
   - Provide requested documents promptly to avoid interruptions.  

---

## Tips to Help You Receive the Full Benefit You’re Eligible For  

| **Tip** | **Why it helps** |
|---------|------------------|
| **File your claim as soon as you become unemployed** | Benefits start after a one‑week waiting period; early filing reduces the gap. |
| **Certify every week (or every two weeks) on time** | Late certifications can cause payment delays or missed weeks. |
| **Report all earnings accurately** | Under‑reporting can lead to overpayments that you’ll have to repay later; over‑reporting can cause a temporary reduction but keeps the claim valid. |
| **Keep a job‑search log** | The EDD may ask for proof of your job‑search activities; a simple spreadsheet or notebook works. |
| **Use direct deposit** | Payments arrive faster than mailed checks. |
| **Check for any “extended” benefits** during state‑wide emergencies (e.g., natural disasters) | Extensions can add weeks of UI beyond the standard 26 weeks. |
| **Ask your county EDD office about “partial unemployment”** if you’re working reduced hours | You may still qualify for a partial benefit, which can increase total income. |

> **Important:** While these steps can help you receive the maximum amount you’re eligible for, the exact weekly benefit is set by the EDD based on your past earnings. No action can increase the statutory maximum beyond what the state allows.

---

## Other Programs That May Be Helpful While You’re Unemployed  

| **Program** | **What it Provides** | **How to Apply** |
|-------------|----------------------|------------------|
| **CalWORKs (California Work Opportunity and Responsibility to Kids)** | Cash assistance for low‑income families with children, plus job‑training services. | Apply at your **County Human Services Agency** or online at [CalWORKs](https://www.cdss.ca.gov/calworks). |
| **CalFresh (SNAP)** | Monthly food benefits to buy groceries. | Apply online at [GetCalFresh](https://www.getcalfresh.org) or at a local **County Social Services Office**. |
| **Medi‑Cal** | Free or low‑cost health coverage for low‑income adults and children. | Apply online at [Medi‑Cal](https://www.dhcs.ca.gov/services/medi-cal/Pages/Apply.aspx) or through your county. |
| **General Assistance (GA)** | Cash aid for adults without other income sources, administered by counties. | Contact your **County Social Services Office** for eligibility and application. |
| **Workforce Development Programs** (e.g., **America’s Job Center of California**) | Job‑search assistance, training, and sometimes wage subsidies. | Find your nearest center at [Job Center Locator](https://www.caljobs.ca.gov). |

---

## Timeline Overview (Typical)  

| **Action** | **When it Happens** |
|------------|---------------------|
| File initial UI claim | As soon as you are unemployed (online, phone, or in‑person). |
| Waiting week (no payment) | Week 1 after claim filing. |
| First benefit payment | Usually within 2‑3 weeks after the waiting week, if weekly certifications are on time. |
| Weekly certifications | Every Monday (or as directed) for each week you want payment. |
| Possible extension requests | During or after the 26‑week period, if a state emergency is declared. |

*Exact dates can vary by county and by how quickly you submit required documents.*

---

## Getting Help

Unemployment Insurance: 
- What is it? Temporary income when you lose your job (or had hours reduced) through no fault of your own. 
- How much can I get? You get from $40 to $450 each week, depending on how much you earned in the past 18 months. EDD has an Unemployment Benefit Calculator to help you estimate how much you might get before you apply.

- You may also be able to attend school or training while receiving unemployment benefits. Learn more about California Training Benefits here: https://edd.ca.gov/en/unemployment/
- Am I eligible? You need to have all of the following to get unemployment benefits: Social Security number, authorization to work in the US (if not a US citizen), have earned a minimum amount of money over the past 18 months (called base period), be totally or partially unemployed through no fault of your own, and be physically able to, available for and looking for work each week and ready / willing to accept work right away
- What documents you need to make applying faster: 
--Personal Information (SSN, photo ID, other identity documentation like a W2 or bill)
--Past 18 Months of Employment Information (Employer names, mailing and physical addresses, dates worked, total income before taxes and deductions (gross wages), hours worked, and how you were paid (e.g., weekly or monthly)
--Most Recent Employer Information (Employer name, address, and phone number and your immediate supervisor, date you last worked, and total income before taxes and deductions (gross wages) in the last week (Sun - Sat) you worked

--Citizenship (if non-US citizen, you’ll need your USCIS document, such as your Permanent Resident Card, Employment Authorization Card, or Refugee Travel Document)

Step 1: Get all the information and documents above together. 
Step 2: Apply online on California's EDD website, call by phone 1-800-300-5616 M-F 8am to 5pm PT or apply by fax or mail 
Step 3: After you apply, you have 21 days to sign up for and upload your resume to CalJOBS. 
Step 4: Review Benefit Documents - 2 weeks after you apply, California EDD may ask for more information. They will also send you key documents about your benefits. Details below: 
Notice of Unemployment Insurance Claim Filed (DE 1101CLMT): This is a summary of your claim information. It explains how to correct any errors to avoid payment delays.

Notice of Unemployment Insurance Award (DE 429Z): This form explains what benefits you can expect, and how to avoid payment delays. If any information is wrong, follow the instructions and appeal in writing within 30 days to avoid payment delays.
Unemployment Insurance Benefits: What You Need to Know (DE 1275B): This provides you a link to a document that explains how you can avoid payment delays by accurately certifying for benefits every two weeks.
Continued Claim (DE 4581): You can use this form to certify by paper, but the process is much slower. Save time and do it online at myEDD or by phone. You’ll certify for benefits every two weeks.
Request for Identity Verification (DE 1326C): If you applied by phone, fax, or mail (or we can’t immediately verify your identity), you’ll receive this form. Visit Respond to Your Request for Identity Verification to learn how to avoid further delays.

## 2. Unemployment Insurance (UI)

### What It Is  
State‑run cash assistance for people who lost work through no fault of their own.

### Basic Eligibility  
| Requirement | Details |
|-------------|---------|
| **Job loss** | Laid off, reduced hours, or employer closed. |
| **Earned wages** | Must have earned enough wages during the “base period” (usually the first 4 of the last 5 completed quarters). |
| **Able & available** | Must be physically able to work and actively looking for a job. |
| **Legal work status** | Must be a U.S. citizen, permanent resident, or have a valid work permit. |

### How to Apply  
1. **Create an account** on **[EDD UI Online](https://edd.ca.gov/Unemployment/UI_Online.htm)**.  
2. **Complete the application** (about 30 min).  
3. **Submit required documents** (see below).  
4. **Certify weekly** to keep benefits flowing.

### Documents You May Need  
- Last employer’s name, address, and dates of employment.  
- Most recent pay stub or W‑2.  
- Driver’s license or ID number.  
- Bank account info for direct deposit (optional but faster).

### Timeline  
- **Initial claim**: Usually processed within **10‑14 days** after you submit everything.  
- **Weekly certification**: Must be done **every 2 weeks** to receive payment.

## 3. Health Coverage

### a. Covered California (Marketplace)  
- **What:** Subsidized health insurance plans.  
- **Eligibility:** Income up to 600 % of the Federal Poverty Level (FPL).  
- **How to Apply:** Visit **[CoveredCA.org](https://www.coveredca.com)** and fill out an application. You’ll need recent pay stubs or a letter showing loss of income.

### b. Medi‑Cal (California’s Medicaid)

- **How to Apply:** Call **1‑800‑541‑5555** or apply online at **[GetMediCal.org](https://www.getmedicaid.org)**.

### Timeline  
- **CalFresh**: Usually approved within **7‑14 days**.  
- **GA/County Relief**: Decision time varies; many counties aim for **30 days**.

1. **Call 988** (or text 741741) if you need immediate emotional support.  
2. **Apply for Unemployment** on the EDD website today.  
3. **Apply for health coverage** (Medi‑Cal or Covered California) within the next 7 days.  
4. **Submit a CalFresh application** online; you may qualify right away.  
5. **Contact your County Human Services Agency** for GA, ERAP, or any county‑specific rapid assistance.

["## Learn about COBRA insurance and how to get coverage

"## How does COBRA insurance work?

- COBRA applies to most private sector businesses with 20 or more employees. It requires an employer's group health insurance plan to continue after qualifying life events. These include:
- Termination or a reduction of a covered employee's hours
- Divorce or legal separation from a covered employee
- Death of a covered employee
- Medicare eligibility for a covered employee
- Loss of a child's or dependent's health insurance coverage under the plan
- Qualified beneficiaries under COBRA include:
- An employee
- Spouse
- Former spouses
- Dependent children
- The amount of time COBRA benefits last depends on the qualifying life event you experience. In some cases, it may be for 36 months. If your hours were reduced or your job was terminated, you can receive COBRA benefits for 18 months.", 
"## Find out if you are eligible for COBRA

- COBRA eligibility has three basic requirements that must be met for you to get a continuation of coverage:
- Your group health plan must be covered by COBRA.
- A qualifying event must occur.
- You must be a qualified beneficiary for that event.", 
"## How to get COBRA coverage

When a qualifying life event happens, you or your employer will notify the health plan. The plan will send an election notice that you will have 60 days to respond to. If you elect to take COBRA coverage, your employer may pay a portion of or the full amount of your insurance premium.

- If you currently have COBRA coverage

How to apply: Applying online is fastest (takes about 30 minutes) on coveredca.com. You can also get free help locally from a certified enroller or apply by phone (takes abuot 1 hour). You can also complete a paper application and mail it in but processing may take a bit longer. 
Gathering these documents ahead of time can make the application process go faster: 
Covered California compares information you put in your application with government data sources. If the data does not match, Covered California will need additional documents from you such as the following: proof of income, SSN, identity, citizenship / immigration status, proof of lack of minimum essential health coverage (this can be a certificate from an insurance company showing end date of your previous coverage, an employer statement saying they no longer offer this kind of health coverage, etc.). Keeping your benefits: 
You must report any changes in your life situation to (for example, address, family size, income) within 30 days. 
Renewal is in the fall of each year and goes to the end of the calendar year. You'll get notified by Covered California when it's time. 


## COBRA insurance 
COBRA is another temporary option for health coverage. It applies to most private companies with 20 or more employees. It requires that the employer's group health insurance plan continues after qualifying life events such as: 
- Termination of reduction in employee hours 
- Divorce or legal separation from a covered employee
- Death of an employee
- Medicare eligibility for a employee
- Loss of a child or dependent's health coverage under the plan 
How long do COBRA benefits last? 
This depends on the qualifying life event. Some times this is 36 months or 3 years. If you are on COBRA because your employer reduced your hours or terminated your job, you could receive COBRA for 18 months or 1.5 years. 
Eligibility for COBRA: 
- Your group health plan must be covered by COBRA
- A qualifying life event must occur 
- You must be a qualified beneficiary for the event.

- Your employer notifies your health plan when a qualifying life event happens.
- Keep an eye out for an election notice from the health plan - you will have 60 days to respond to it.

There are also options for help with medical bills even if you don't have insurance or are under-insured (you have healthcare needs that are not covered by your plan):

Children are always counted as part of the household. | | **What counts as income?** | Wages, unemployment insurance (UI), severance pay, and most other cash benefits. Some income is **partially excluded** (e.g., a portion of UI). | | **What counts as resources?** | Savings, checking accounts, and some other assets. Most households can have up to **$2,500** in resources (higher for seniors). | | **How fast can you get help?** | Standard processing: 7‑14 days.
Emergency allotment (if you have no food at home): **within 3 days** of a complete application. | | **Where to apply?** | Online at **[GetCalFresh.org](https://www.getcalfresh.org)**, by phone, or in person at your county social services office. | --- ## How UI and Severance Pay Affect Eligibility | Type of payment | Effect on CalFresh eligibility | |-----------------|---------------------------------| | **Unemployment Insurance (UI)** | UI is counted as income, but **the first $100 of UI each month is excluded**. The rest is counted at the normal rate. | | **Severance pay** | Treated like regular wages. It is counted as income in the month you receive it. If the severance is a lump sum, it may push you over the income limit for that month, but you can still qualify in later months once the money is spent. | | **Both together** | Both are added together (after the $100 UI exclusion) to determine monthly income. Most counties follow the same state rules, but **some have different appointment wait times or additional local forms**. - If you move **out of state**, you will need to end your California case and apply for SNAP in the new state. --- ## Steps to Apply (Simple Checklist) 1. **Gather documents** - Photo ID (driver’s license, state ID, or passport) - Proof of residence (lease, utility bill, or a letter from your mom) - Recent pay stubs or proof of UI/severance (E‑Verify, UI award letter) - Bank statements (showing savings) - Social Security numbers for all household members 2. **Create an account** at **[GetCalFresh.org](https://www.getcalfresh.org)** or call **1‑877‑847‑3663**. 3. **Complete the online application** (or fill out a paper form if you prefer). 4. **Submit required documents** - Upload scans/photos online, or bring them to the county office. 5. **Interview** - Usually a short phone or video interview. - If you need an interpreter, request one when you apply. 6. **Receive a decision** - You’ll get a notice by mail or online. - If approved, you’ll receive an EBT card in the mail (usually within 7 days). 7. **Report any changes** (new job, change in income, move, etc.) promptly to keep benefits accurate. --- ## Timeline at a Glance | Action | Approx. ["## Learn about COBRA insurance and how to get coverage

- COBRA, the Consolidated Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act, lets qualified workers keep their group health insurance for a limited time after a change in eligibility.", 
"## How does COBRA insurance work?

- COBRA applies to most private sector businesses with 20 or more employees. It requires an employer's group health insurance plan to continue after qualifying life events. These include:
- Termination or a reduction of a covered employee's hours
- Divorce or legal separation from a covered employee
- Death of a covered employee
- Medicare eligibility for a covered employee
- Loss of a child's or dependent's health insurance coverage under the plan
- Qualified beneficiaries under COBRA include:
- An employee
- Spouse
- Former spouses
- Dependent children
- The amount of time COBRA benefits last depends on the qualifying life event you experience. In some cases, it may be for 36 months. If your hours were reduced or your job was terminated, you can receive COBRA benefits for 18 months.", 
"## Find out if you are eligible for COBRA

- COBRA eligibility has three basic requirements that must be met for you to get a continuation of coverage:
- Your group health plan must be covered by COBRA.
- A qualifying event must occur.
- You must be a qualified beneficiary for that event.", 
"## How to get COBRA coverage

When a qualifying life event happens, you or your employer will notify the health plan. The plan will send an election notice that you will have 60 days to respond to. If you elect to take COBRA coverage, your employer may pay a portion of or the full amount of your insurance premium.
- Contact your employer’s health insurance plan administrator with questions about COBRA, including:
- If you currently have COBRA coverage
- When your COBRA coverage will begin
- How long the coverage may last"],

["## Steps to take for charity care or financial help with medical bills

How to apply: Applying online is fastest (takes about 30 minutes) on coveredca.com. You can also get free help locally from a certified enroller or apply by phone (takes abuot 1 hour). You can also complete a paper application and mail it in but processing may take a bit longer.

Keeping your benefits:

## COBRA insurance 
COBRA is another temporary option for health coverage. It applies to most private companies with 20 or more employees. It requires that the employer's group health insurance plan continues after qualifying life events such as: 
- Termination of reduction in employee hours 
- Divorce or legal separation from a covered employee
- Death of an employee
- Medicare eligibility for a employee
- Loss of a child or dependent's health coverage under the plan 
How long do COBRA benefits last? 
This depends on the qualifying life event. Some times this is 36 months or 3 years. If you are on COBRA because your employer reduced your hours or terminated your job, you could receive COBRA for 18 months or 1.5 years. 
Eligibility for COBRA:

- A qualifying life event must occur

## You May Be Able to Get Help

I’m sorry you’re going through this.  Below are the main programs in California that can help with **food, health care, and basic bills**.  Most of them are open to people who are not U.S. citizens **if you have a lawful immigration status** (green card, work permit, refugee/asylee status, etc.).  Each county runs the programs slightly differently, so you’ll need to check with your local office for exact details.

| What you need help with | Main program(s) | Who can apply (basic rule) | What you’ll need to show |
|--------------------------|----------------|----------------------------|--------------------------|
| **Food** (groceries, meals) | **CalFresh** (California SNAP) | Lawful residents (including many immigrants) | ID, proof of residence, income & expenses, household size |
| **Health care** (doctor visits, prescriptions) | **Medi‑Cal** (California Medicaid) | Lawful residents; some programs also cover certain undocumented children | ID, proof of residence, income, immigration documents |
| **Cash for rent, utilities, other bills** | **General Assistance (GA)** or **County Relief** | Varies by county; many counties help low‑income families regardless of citizenship | ID, proof of residence, income, rent/utility bills |
| **Kids’ nutrition at school** | **Free/Reduced‑Price Meals** | All children who qualify for CalFresh or meet income test | Proof of school enrollment, income info |
| **Pregnant women & infants** | **WIC** (Women, Infants, Children) | Lawful residents; some counties serve undocumented pregnant women | ID, proof of residence, pregnancy/infant info |
| **Unemployment benefits** | **UI (Unemployment Insurance)** | Must have a valid work permit and have earned enough wages; most undocumented workers are not eligible | Recent pay stubs, employment history |

### 1. CalFresh (Food Assistance)

- **What it does:** Gives you a monthly benefit to buy groceries.
- **Eligibility basics:** Household income must be at most 200 % of the federal poverty level. Many immigrants qualify after a **5‑year waiting period**, but **qualified refugees, asylees, and certain other statuses are exempt**.
- **How to apply:**  
  1. Call your county’s CalFresh office or apply online at the **[California Department of Social Services portal](https://www.getcalfresh.org/)**.  
  2. Fill out the application (you can do it in English or Spanish).  
  3. Submit copies of ID, proof of residence (utility bill or lease), and recent pay stubs or bank statements.
- **Timeline:** Most counties decide within **30 days**; you can get an **emergency cash advance** while you wait.

### 2. Medi‑Cal (Health Coverage)

- **What it does:** Covers doctor visits, hospital care, prescriptions, and some dental services.
- **Eligibility basics:** Income must be at or below **138 % of the federal poverty level**. Lawful residents (including many immigrants) qualify; children are often covered even if the parent’s status is limited.
- **How to apply:**  
  1. Call your county’s **Human Services Agency** or apply online at **[Covered California – Medi‑Cal enrollment](https://www.coveredca.com/medi-cal/)**.  
  2. Provide ID, immigration documents, proof of residence, and income information.
- **Timeline:** Usually **within 30 days** of submitting a complete application. You may receive **temporary coverage** while your case is processed.

### 3. General Assistance (County Relief)

- **What it does:** Gives cash help for rent, utilities, or other essential bills when you have no other income.
- **Eligibility basics:** Varies a lot by county. Most counties require you to be a **California resident** and have **very low or no income**. Some counties accept undocumented residents; others limit assistance to lawful residents.
- **How to apply:**  
  1. Contact your **County Social Services Office** (search “General Assistance + [your county]”).  
  2. Bring ID, proof of residence, rent/utility bills, and any income records.
- **Timeline:** Decision time can range from **2 weeks to 2 months** depending on the county.

### 4. WIC (Women, Infants, Children)

- **What it does:** Provides nutritious foods, nutrition counseling, and breastfeeding support.
- **Eligibility basics:** Pregnant, postpartum, or breastfeeding women and children under 5 who meet income guidelines (usually ≤ 185 % of the federal poverty level). Lawful residents qualify; many counties also serve undocumented pregnant women.
- **How to apply:** Call your local **WIC office** or visit **[WIC California](https://www.cdph.ca.gov/Programs/CFH/DMCA/Pages/WIC.aspx)**.

### 5. Free/Reduced‑Price School Meals

- **What it does:** Gives kids free breakfast and lunch at school.
- **Eligibility basics:** Same income test as CalFresh. If your child qualifies for CalFresh, they automatically qualify for free meals.
- **How to apply:** Talk to your child’s school counselor or use the **[School Meals Application](https://www.cde.ca.gov/ls/ss/)**.

---

## Steps to Get Started

1. **Gather basic documents** (you’ll need most of these for every program):
   - Photo ID (driver’s license, state ID, or passport)
   - Proof of California residence (utility bill, lease, or mail addressed to you)
   - Recent pay stubs, bank statements, or any proof of income (or a statement that you have no income)
   - Immigration documents that show lawful status (green card, work permit, refugee/asylee paperwork, etc.)
   - Social Security number (if you have one) or Individual Taxpayer Identification Number (ITIN)

2. **Make a list of the programs you want to apply for** (CalFresh, Medi‑Cal, GA, etc.).

3. **Contact your county’s Human Services Agency** (or use the online portals).  The staff can walk you through each application and tell you exactly which documents are needed.

4. **Submit the applications**—many can be done online, but you can also apply in person or by phone if you prefer.

5. **Follow up** if you haven’t heard back within the stated timeline.  Keep copies of everything you submit.

---

## Will Your Information Be Shared?

- **Privacy is protected by law.**  California agencies must follow the **California Confidentiality of Medical Information Act (CMIA)** and **Federal privacy rules**.  
- Your personal data is **shared only with other state or federal agencies that need it to determine eligibility** (e.g., the Department of Health Care Services for Medi‑Cal).

- If you have concerns, ask the caseworker to explain how your data will be used before you sign any forms.

|----------|----------------|-------------------|

| **Emergency Rental Assistance Program (ERAP)** | One‑time help paying rent or utilities if you’re facing a crisis. | Check your county’s website for the current ERAP portal. |
| **Legal Aid Society / Immigration Legal Services** | Free or low‑cost help with immigration status, which can affect benefit eligibility. | Find a local office at **[LawHelpCA.org](https://www.lawhelpca.org/)**. |
| **211 California** | Phone or online service that can connect you to local food banks, shelters, and other assistance. | Dial **211** or visit **[211.org](https://www.211.org/)**. |
| **Community Action Agencies** | Offer a range of services (energy assistance, job training, food programs). | Search “Community Action Agency + [your county]”. |

## COBRA insurance 
COBRA is another temporary option for health coverage. It applies to most private companies with 20 or more employees. It requires that the employer's group health insurance plan continues after qualifying life events such as: 
- Termination of reduction in employee hours 
- Divorce or legal separation from a covered employee
- Death of an employee
- Medicare eligibility for a employee
- Loss of a child or dependent's health coverage under the plan

- A qualifying life event must occur

- Keep an eye out for an election notice from the health plan - you will have 60 days to respond to it.
